## Buenos Aires with Lezama and Palermo parks: a private excursion

A private excursion around [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) reveals the city through its historic squares, central avenues and leafy neighborhoods. It is particularly appealing if you want to explore more than famous facades and tango districts and see how Argentinians use their parks and public spaces.

We offer **a private half-day itinerary with a Russian-speaking guide**. It connects Plaza de Mayo, Avenida 9 de Julio and the Obelisk, La Boca, San Telmo, Recoleta, Puerto Madero, Lezama Park and Tres de Febrero Park. **The services of a Russian-speaking guide** are included; a separate fixed price, transport and admission tickets have not been confirmed in the excursion's terms.

## The capital's main squares and avenues

The city's historic heart is **Plaza de Mayo**, surrounded by important government and colonial buildings. From here, it is natural to explore the capital's later growth: Avenida 9 de Julio, the Obelisk, Avenida Corrientes and Avenida de Mayo show a very different period in the city's development.

The itinerary also includes Plaza San Martín and Plaza del Congreso. These stops make it possible to compare monuments and public spaces connected with the formation of the Argentine state.

On **Avenida 9 de Julio**, the 67-meter-high Obelisk stands out as one of the city's most recognizable landmarks. It is an excellent introduction to the city and its central geography, although the time spent there depends on the chosen order of stops.

## La Boca, San Telmo and Monserrat

**La Boca** is associated with port history, colorful houses and football culture. [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/) retains the atmosphere of old streets, squares and antique shops. Monserrat is part of the historic capital, with institutions, churches and buildings from different eras.

Together, these neighborhoods show why Buenos Aires cannot be described by a single architectural style. The route moves from old stone facades and small squares to broad traffic arteries and modern developments.

Depending on available time, the city excursion may involve driving past or walking around attractions. **A list of neighborhoods does not imply entry into every museum or church**; any such visits must be agreed separately.

## Lezama Park and Tres de Febrero Park

**Lezama Park** lies beside historic neighborhoods in the south of the city and offers a peaceful green contrast to San Telmo's busy streets. It is loved for its old trees, pathways and the historic urban surroundings. For visitors, it is a chance to see Buenos Aires as a place where residents take their everyday walks.

**Tres de Febrero Park**, in Palermo, is known for its extensive green spaces and ponds. Walking paths run throughout the area, making it one of the Argentine capital's most prominent landscaped parks.

These 2 parks are in different parts of the city. Visiting both in half a day requires a sensible sequence of transfers. It is therefore worth discussing which park matters most for a longer walk and which would be better for a short stop and photographs.

## Palermo, Recoleta and Puerto Madero

**Palermo** is attractive for its leafy streets, residential blocks and modern cultural spaces. **Recoleta** is known for historic facades, its cemetery and museums. In modern **Puerto Madero**, former port docks have become a district of waterfront promenades, offices and restaurants.

The final portion of the route lists the financial and business center and a football stadium. However, **the particular stadium and whether it can be visited inside are not specified**. Do not automatically expect access to changing rooms, a club museum or the stands.

A separate **tango show** is likewise not part of the confirmed stops: it is a distinct evening program offered by Ada Tours.

## Private half-day tour or a 3-hour group excursion?

Our catalog also includes a [3-hour group sightseeing excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-three-hours-russian-group/). It provides a first look at the main neighborhoods in limited time with a group. The **private half-day** option allows the introduction to focus on your interests, with more attention to green spaces.

| Option | Key feature |
|---|---|
| [Group, 3 hours](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-three-hours-russian-group/) | Brief first introduction |
| [Private, half-day](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-city-parks-russian-private/) | Parks and a personal pace |

Here, **half-day** describes the format, not a precise promise of a fixed number of hours. Preferences for walking time, stops and photography breaks should be discussed in advance.

## Frequently asked questions about the private excursion

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide?

Yes. **A Russian-speaking guide's services** are included.

### Is transport included?

Guide services are included, but transport has not been confirmed as a separately paid service. Its availability and format should be clarified when arranging the tour.

### How long does the excursion last?

The format is described as **half a day**. The excursion's terms do not specify an exact number of hours.

### Can we visit a stadium inside?

Only if separately confirmed. The program mentions a football stadium without naming it or guaranteeing entry.

### Which is better for someone interested in urban history and nature?

If you want to see the center and several different green neighborhoods, the private excursion featuring Lezama and Palermo offers a more suitable selection of stops. For broader historical subjects, compare the [“Culture and History”](/interests/culture-and-history/) collection.

## Buenos Aires food tour: meat, desserts and wine

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), discovering local cuisine works well as a dedicated excursion. On our itinerary, you first visit a restaurant serving grilled meat, then taste traditional desserts and Argentine wines. **Duration: approximately 6 hours.** Over that time, you experience 3 different food traditions rather than simply having lunch in one restaurant.

The specific restaurants, menu and order of individual tastings need to be agreed separately. Plan around the structure of the food itinerary, then confirm its details before your trip.

## Argentine asado and parrilla culture

Meat cooked over an open flame has an important place in Argentine cuisine. *Asado* describes both the cooking method and the shared meal. A *Parrilla* is a grill and also a type of restaurant where meat is cooked on a grate or brazier.

Buenos Aires has traditional parrillas as well as restaurants offering modern interpretations of meat dishes. Familiar Argentine cuts include *bife de chorizo*, *entraña* and *ojo de bife*. Knowing these names may help you read menus, but it **does not mean** that each cut is served on the Ada Tours excursion.

The first stage of the food tour is about understanding how local restaurant culture differs from a typical tourist dinner. The cooking method, level of doneness, presentation and side dishes all matter. If you do not eat meat, let us know in advance: an alternative menu cannot be regarded as confirmed until it has been agreed.

## Desserts: from dulce de leche to city pastry shops

The next part of the itinerary focuses on traditional sweets. One of Argentina's most recognizable flavors is *dulce de leche*, a thick milk caramel. It is used in cakes, *alfajores* biscuits and many homemade and restaurant desserts.

Buenos Aires' food culture developed under the influence of European migration, particularly Italian and Spanish culinary traditions. The city is therefore known for more than meat: pastry shops, cafés, ice cream and baked goods are popular. The dessert portion of the excursion reveals this side of the capital.

The specific selection of sweets is determined by the agreed program. *Alfajores* and dulce de leche are useful examples of local cuisine, but they cannot be promised as required tasting items without a menu.

## Argentine wines and how to approach them

The wine portion complements the meat and dessert experiences with an introduction to Argentine winemaking. The country's best-known association with red wine is Malbec, particularly prominent in Mendoza. Argentine wines nevertheless vary by grape variety, region, aging and style, so a tasting is more interesting than simply choosing “red or white.”

During this experience, pay attention to aroma, acidity, body and food pairings. The exact wines, serving sizes and availability of non-alcoholic alternatives need to be confirmed for your chosen date. Our itinerary includes wine tasting, but **the specific wineries and labels must be agreed**.

If you prefer not to drink alcohol, or have age-related restrictions or personal preferences, it is better to discuss them before the excursion rather than during the tasting.

## Why set aside 6 hours for the food experience?

A six-hour food excursion needs time for several stages. Placing it between a sightseeing tour and an evening event creates a full day, particularly if the restaurants are far apart. The itinerary must account for travel distances, service times and the possibility of a short break.

Our [Buenos Aires city guide](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) describes La Boca, San Telmo, the historic center and other neighborhoods. It would be incorrect to assume in advance that the food itinerary visits those particular districts: restaurant locations are determined separately.

There is no need to select restaurants solely from popular rankings either. For this excursion, the agreed progression from meat to desserts and wine is far more important than a list of fashionable addresses.

## Comparing a gaucho day and an evening tango show

On the [Santa Susana ranch excursion](/argentina/santa-susana-ranch/santa-susana-gaucho-day-lunch/), a traditional barbecue forms part of a day in the countryside, where visitors also encounter gaucho culture and folklore. On the city food tour, the cuisine itself is the main focus.

The [“Tango Porteño” dinner show](/argentina/buenos-aires/tango-porteno-dinner-show/) offers a third format: the evening centers on a stage performance accompanied by dinner. If you are spending several days in the capital, combining these formats reveals different sides of Argentina without repeating the same excursion.

For food lovers, there is also a broader collection of [food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/). It includes winemaking and regional dishes, while this six-hour product focuses on Buenos Aires.

## Frequently asked questions about the food excursion

### How long is the food tour?

Approximately 6 hours. The itinerary covers grilled meat, traditional desserts and Argentine wines.

### Which restaurants are on the itinerary?

The canonical excursion description does not specify restaurant names. They should be agreed when choosing a date and planning the program.

### Do you have to drink wine?

The itinerary includes a wine tasting, but personal preferences and non-alcoholic alternatives should be discussed in advance. No single substitute has been confirmed for every guest.

### Is this suitable for a first introduction to Argentina?

Yes, if you are interested in the country's flavors and are ready to devote a separate half-day to them. For a general introduction to the city, add [Buenos Aires sightseeing experiences](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) rather than replacing the food itinerary with them.

## Tours featuring a Buenos Aires food excursion

A trip to [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) can focus on historic neighborhoods, tango and Argentine cuisine. For travelers particularly interested in the country's flavors, we offer a [Buenos Aires food excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-food-tour/). The excursion has three parts: a restaurant serving meat cooked over fire, traditional desserts and a tasting of Argentine wines. The estimated duration is **around 6 hours**.

This is a complete food experience, not a brief café stop between landmarks. Different flavors are explored in sequence, and time spent at the table occupies a significant part of the day. That is why, when choosing a longer tour, it matters what else is scheduled for that date.

## Which journey includes the excursion?

The [18-day “Argentina, Chile, Bolivia and Patagonia” journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) includes the food tour during the stay in the Argentine capital. On **day 13**, travelers first take a sightseeing excursion around Buenos Aires, including La Boca and San Telmo, and then join the food tour. The following day involves a flight to Bariloche.

This positioning is important for planning. Travelers discover the city's architecture and history before turning to its cuisine. However, combining sightseeing with a tasting program lasting approximately 6 hours requires agreed start times, transfers and an end-of-day schedule. **Dates, restaurant-stop times and the actual scope of services must be confirmed for the chosen option** so they do not conflict with the evening itinerary.

The longer journey is chosen for its multiple countries and varied natural regions, while the food excursion becomes its Buenos Aires episode. If your main aim is restaurants and wineries, compare [food and wine tours in Argentina](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/): the multi-day itineraries in that collection may be quite different.

## What introduces travelers to Argentine cuisine?

**Grilled meat.** The Argentine *parrilla* is a tradition of cooking meat on a grill or brazier. Buenos Aires has classic steak restaurants as well as modern interpretations. The excursion introduces meat dishes but does not commit to a specific restaurant, particular cuts or serving sizes.

**Desserts.** Argentine cuisine features sweets made with *dulce de leche*, as well as alfajores and ice cream. The separate excursion mentions tasting traditional desserts. The specific items and stops depend on the agreed option, so it would be wrong to promise a particular pastry shop in advance.

**Wine.** A tasting of Argentine wines completes this introduction to national cuisine. When selecting drinks, consider the participants' preferences: an interest in Malbec, white wines or non-alcoholic alternatives. The exact labels and wineries have not been specified; the excursion takes place in Buenos Aires and should not automatically be equated with a trip through Mendoza's vineyards.

## Scheduling the food portion

In [historic San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/) and other city districts, it is easy to linger over a walk, but the food tour requires time for each tasting. If it follows a substantial sightseeing excursion, agree the sequence of meetings and meals in advance. Avoid planning another large dinner immediately after a long food experience.

If street food, independent market exploration or a particular restaurant is your priority, those are different formats to discuss separately. The current [Ada Tours excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-food-tour/) specifically combines meat, desserts and wine; it is not an unrestricted visit to all the city's famous restaurants.

When choosing a longer itinerary, compare the length of its stop in the capital with the days allotted to subsequent regions. The [Argentina tours page](/argentina/tour/) includes itineraries of various kinds, while this selection shows tours that include the chosen standalone food excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about the food tour

### How much time is needed for the Buenos Aires food excursion?

The duration is **around 6 hours**. If sightseeing is also planned that day, coordinate the timing and transfers for both activities.

### Does it include a trip to wineries?

The food excursion description confirms Argentine wine tasting during a visit to Buenos Aires. It does not specify a trip to vineyards or individual producers. Compare winery itineraries separately.

### Can I choose a restaurant and menu?

The conditions and set of stops must be agreed for the specific itinerary. The published food tour describes three tasting themes but does not name mandatory restaurants, a fixed menu or the cost of individual substitutions.

## Half-day Buenos Aires sightseeing excursion with guide and lunch

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), it is difficult to choose a single route for a first introduction: historic neighborhoods, wide avenues, theaters and museums are spread across the large city. Ada Tours' half-day sightseeing excursion introduces the architecture and atmosphere of the Argentine capital with a guide.

Our excursion includes **a half-day tour, entrance tickets listed in the itinerary, lunch and transfers**. The exact stops are agreed when booking. It therefore helps to decide in advance whether you are more interested in the colonial history of the center, La Boca's brightly colored streets, cultural San Telmo or the architecture of affluent neighborhoods.

## What can you see in different parts of Buenos Aires?

The city center is associated with [Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada and historic streets](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). This is a good area to discover the country's political history and major civic buildings. Avenida 9 de Julio and the Obelisk show a completely different side of the capital: broad traffic spaces and expansive urban views.

La Boca is known for the colorful facades of Caminito, immigration history and street art. San Telmo is older and more intimate, with antique shops, architectural details and tango's musical tradition. Both neighborhoods are described in detail on Buenos Aires' official tourist website.

These are **options to consider**, not a list of mandatory stops on this particular excursion. Our route introduces neighborhoods, historic avenues and architecture but does not specify visits to every place mentioned. If a certain museum, square or district is essential to you, arrange to include it in the itinerary in advance.

## Why is the half-day format convenient?

A half-day makes it easier to focus on several related sights rather than trying to see every neighborhood in the capital. The guide explains the city's geography, history and architectural differences, while transfers reduce the time spent traveling independently. The itinerary also leaves time for an evening activity or a walk on your own.

| Priority | What to agree with the guide |
|---|---|
| Historic center | Squares and buildings accessible for visits |
| Architecture | Neighborhoods and notable facades |
| Museums | Specific tickets and admission times |
| City life | Walking stops and time for a stroll |

A half-day tour is particularly useful at the beginning of a longer journey through Argentina, when the overview helps you choose places to revisit on your own. At the same time, “half-day” does not mean a universal number of hours for every date and group: meeting arrangements, traffic and selected sights must be agreed separately.

## What is included in the Ada Tours excursion?

The program explicitly includes guide services, entrance tickets for included attractions, lunch and necessary transfers. **Drinks are not included** unless separately agreed.

Including tickets does not mean access to every museum in Buenos Aires: paid admissions depend on the agreed stops. Likewise, a particular attraction with restricted opening hours cannot be promised if it is not in the confirmed itinerary.

Guide arrangements and language should be confirmed when booking separately. This excursion does not specify a fixed guide language; it would be incorrect to promise a Russian-speaking guide or a private car without an appropriate agreement.

## Preparing for a city walk

Buenos Aires' weather and temperatures vary by season, and distances between neighborhoods can be substantial. Comfortable shoes help even on excursions with transfers, because historic districts are best explored on foot. For ticketed attractions, consider opening times and any need to book a specific entry slot.

Groups should agree their main stops before traveling. If participants are interested in different topics, a brief overview works best when built around common priorities, leaving specialized museums or food itineraries for separate outings.

If a cultural program is your priority, consider [Argentina tours featuring “Culture and History”](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/). This city excursion complements them but does not replace dedicated days in other regions.

## What can you combine with a Buenos Aires excursion?

On the [6-day “Argentina: Buenos Aires, Tigre and Gaucho Traditions” journey](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/), sightseeing takes place **during the day on day 2**, and in the evening participants attend the [Michelangelo tango show with dinner](/argentina/buenos-aires/michelangelo-tango-dinner-transfer/).

The following day includes a [trip to Tigre and the Paraná Delta](/argentina/tigre/tigre-parana-delta-half-day-lunch/), a different natural and suburban environment. Spreading these outings across separate days avoids combining the evening show, city sightseeing and river excursion into one continuous activity.

The 6-day tour is designed for a group and has its own conditions for accommodation, transfers and meals. These should not automatically be applied to a standalone half-day excursion, which requires its own list of included services.

## Frequently asked questions about the sightseeing excursion

### How long is the Buenos Aires excursion?

Our excursion lasts **half a day**. The exact start time and overall route are agreed when booking.

### Are lunch and tickets included in the price?

The confirmed excursion includes lunch, admission tickets along the route, guide services and transfers. Drinks are not included unless otherwise agreed.

### Can you choose particular neighborhoods?

The exact city itinerary is agreed in advance. Specify the neighborhoods and sights that interest you most so they can be matched to the half-day format and opening hours.

### Can we attend tango after the excursion?

On Ada Tours' 6-day itinerary, sightseeing and the evening tango performance are scheduled on the same day. The tango show is a separate [Michelangelo excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/michelangelo-tango-dinner-transfer/) with its own included services.

## Tours featuring a half-day Buenos Aires excursion with lunch

A first look at [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) is easy to begin with a sightseeing excursion: historic neighborhoods, broad avenues and architectural landmarks help you get oriented in the capital. The [“Buenos Aires: Half-Day with Guide and Lunch” excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-half-day-lunch/) includes a guide, admission tickets according to the program, transfers and **lunch**.

Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that use this excursion. One active option is [“Argentina in 6 Days: Buenos Aires, Tigre and Gaucho Traditions”](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/). This is a group itinerary with excursions, dinners, a trip to the Paraná Delta and a ranch visit. The tour also includes a day trip across the Río de la Plata to Uruguay.

## What happens on day 2 of the 6-day itinerary?

**Day 1** of the [6-day tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/) is devoted to arrival at Buenos Aires airport, transfer and a welcome dinner. On **day 2**, the group takes a half-day sightseeing excursion around the capital. Guide services, entrance tickets and lunch are included for this excursion.

In the evening, a **Michelangelo tango show with dinner** is planned, with tickets and transfers as specified in the itinerary. This is a separate activity with its own services. Attendance at the tango show should not be attributed to the half-day sightseeing excursion itself, even though both appear on the same day of the longer journey.

The exact streets, sequence of stops and guide language for the [“Half-Day with Guide and Lunch” excursion](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-half-day-lunch/) are confirmed when booking. It is therefore best to rely on the stated duration, format and included services rather than promise specific museums or districts.

## What follows the city day?

**Day 3** focuses on [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) and the Paraná Delta. The itinerary includes a half-day guided excursion with lunch and tickets, followed by dinner at a local restaurant with transfers in the evening. This offers a different urban and natural experience: city buildings give way to river channels and suburban landscapes.

**Day 4** is a trip across the Río de la Plata to [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) in Uruguay. Ferry tickets, excursion guiding and transfers are confirmed for this day. In the evening, travelers return to Buenos Aires for dinner at the hotel.

**Day 5** explores gaucho culture at [Santa Susana Ranch](/argentina/place/santa-susana-ranch/), including traditional activities, folklore and Argentine barbecue. **Day 6** is the airport transfer. Thus, the Buenos Aires excursion with lunch introduces a journey exploring several sides of the region's culture.

## What is actually included in the excursion and the tour?

The two levels of the itinerary have different commitments. The **standalone half-day excursion** specifies a guide, tickets, lunch and transfers according to its route; drinks are included only by separate agreement. The multi-day tour additionally includes airport transfers, the tango show, Tigre, the trip to Uruguay and Santa Susana Ranch.

| Service | Status |
|---|---|
| Guide, tickets, lunch | Included in excursion |
| Tango show with dinner | Included in 6-day tour |
| Accommodation | By arrangement |
| International flights | Separate |

**Accommodation is not automatically included in the 6-day itinerary.** Its calculations explicitly require hotels to be agreed separately. This matters especially for organized groups, where the price for the excursion program and the final trip cost can differ depending on the chosen hotels.

The commercial terms of the stated tour are calculated for a group of **80 participants**. Different group sizes, accommodation formats or additional requirements must be agreed separately. Lunch included in one excursion module does not mean that all meals across every day are paid for; refer to the listed lunches and dinners in the [program](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/).

## Who is this journey suitable for?

The [6-day itinerary](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/) is aimed in part at **corporate groups**. It suits an introduction to the Argentine capital and its surroundings when organizers want to combine group excursions, lunches and evening events.

Food is part of the cultural program here: Argentine barbecue at the ranch, dinner at the tango show and meals included on excursion days. This differs from [standalone Buenos Aires food tours](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-food-tour/), whose main content is dishes, desserts and wine. The presence of the word “lunch” in a title is no reason to substitute one product for the other.

For travel focused only on the city, start with the [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/); for programs centered on cultural experiences, see [culture and history journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours with a Buenos Aires excursion and lunch

### Is lunch included in the half-day excursion?

Yes. The [standalone excursion module](/argentina/buenos-aires/buenos-aires-half-day-lunch/) explicitly includes lunch, while drinks require separate agreement.

### Is accommodation included in the 6-day tour?

According to the current [tour description](/argentina/tour/argentina-experience-6-days/), **accommodation is not included without separate agreement**. The selected accommodation is considered when calculating the trip's full cost.

### What is planned after sightseeing in the city?

On day 2, a **tango show with dinner**; on day 3, Tigre and the Paraná Delta; then a trip to Uruguay and an introduction to gaucho traditions.

### Do you need to choose specific Buenos Aires neighborhoods in advance?

The precise sightseeing route is agreed when booking. The current listing confirms a half-day with a guide, tickets, transfers and lunch, but does not specify a full list of neighborhoods and museums.
